scope.description: Same four-node scenario as the executed revision (A bootstrapped with {A,B,C}, snapshot, AddVoter D committed, further commits, A restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs so its configuration is the snapshot's {A,B,C}, B and C and D partitioned so a write lands on only two of four voters), extended with a repair phase: the stale leader A is shut down, B, C and D are reconnected and their timeouts shortened, one of them is elected, that leader appends AddVoter E, A is restarted again on its own stores with the flag still enabled, and the probe waits for the leader to replicate the new configuration entry to A and records A's resulting configuration.
assumptions: The repair phase is only meaningful for the failing mode, so it runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and is skipped in the control mode.
The leader from the correctly configured side can append a configuration change because its membership is the committed one ({A,B,C,D}, quorum three, with A down and the other three reachable).
A is restarted with a fresh transport wired to B, C and D, so the leader can replicate to it exactly as it would after an operator restart.
excluded: No snapshot is installed in the repair phase; the repair observed here is the log-entry path only.
The control mode runs without the repair phase, so its earlier comparisons keep their meaning.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap, real snapshot, real AddVoter with catch-up, real commits, real shutdown and restart of the leader on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real partition, then real shutdown of the stale leader, real election on the correctly configured side, real AddVoter E, real restart of A and real replication of the new configuration entry to it. Nothing is fabricated.

comparisons.description: A restarted leader must not forget a voter whose addition is committed in its own log.
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps all four voters.
An entry whose Apply reported success must be held by a quorum of the configuration committed in the log.
Control: with the committed membership the same partition must make the leader refuse the write.
A later configuration entry replicated by a correctly configured leader must restore the forgotten voter (and add the new one) on the previously stale node.

before.description: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts. A is bootstrapped with voters {A,B,C}, all four run, A snapshots, commits a command, adds D as a voter (committed configuration {A,B,C,D}, quorum three) and commits two further commands. A is restarted on the same stores with RestoreCommittedLogs (case restore_on) or without it (control restore_off), with the other three nodes' timeouts lengthened so the restarted leader wins its re-election. The probe records the restarted leader's configuration against the others, then partitions C and D from A and applies one entry, recording whether the Apply succeeded, the entry index, A's commit and applied indexes, each voter's log tail, and how many of the four committed voters hold the entry.
assumptions: D is caught up before the restart, so the committed configuration genuinely has four voters (quorum three).
C and D are disconnected in both directions, which is a real partition for all Raft traffic; A and B remain connected.
The committed configuration {A,B,C,D} requires three acknowledgements, so an entry held by A and B only is not committed under it.
excluded: No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the explicit disconnection of C and D.
D is kept on the normal restart path (flag disabled) so its own configuration recovery cannot confound the observation.

revision_reason: Adds the repair phase to the same scenario: the stale leader is stopped, the correctly configured members elect one of themselves, that leader appends a further configuration change, and the stale node is restarted on its own stores and observed while the leader replicates the new configuration entry to it. The existing observations and four comparisons are unchanged; one comparison is added for the repair event.
